tickets.title: Build the OpenCode rails-guard plugin MVP (per the opencode-integration design)
tickets.body:
Build the FIRST shippable increment of the OpenCode integration: the in-process rails-guard plugin plus the discovery skill, implementing the unbuilt core of the existing design. This ticket was reconciled (2026-06-27) against substantial prior work on branch `opencode-integration` — DO NOT re-derive the design or rebuild what already exists.

=== AUTHORITATIVE DESIGN (the contract — read first) ===
The full OpenCode integration is already designed on branch `opencode-integration` (NOT yet merged to main):
- docs/opencode-integration-plan.md — the 6-phase (A-F) delivery plan and the in-process hook contract. THIS is the design contract; do not contradict it.
- docs/opencode.md — the adoption guide.
Read both via `git show opencode-integration:docs/opencode-integration-plan.md` and `git show opencode-integration:docs/opencode.md`. Treat their primitive mapping (§3), directory structure (§4.1), hook contract (§4.2), and phased plan (§7) as the spec.

=== WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — DO NOT REBUILD (reconciliation) ===
1. Phase F CI backstop is IMPLEMENTED on `opencode-integration`: docs/ci/rails-guard.yml (hardened: codeowners attestation, signed runner pool, trust-root freeze, monotonic config invariants), scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs (+295), and ~1800 lines of tests (scripts/test/rails-guard-bootstrap-ci.test.mjs, scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs). The unbypassable second enforcement layer therefore ALREADY EXISTS. Do not re-author it. The ONLY deferred CI item relevant here (plan §6.2) is protecting `.opencode/plugin/` and `.opencode/opencode.json` paths — note it as Phase F follow-up; do not implement it in this ticket.
2. @adlc/core (v1.1.0) is published and is the single source of truth for rails logic (plan §6.6). The plugin MUST delegate to it, NOT inline-port the adlc-pi helpers (the duplicated legacy CC/codex hooks are explicitly flagged as tech debt to remove).

=== RESOLVED OpenCode plugin API (P1 research + plan, pin in ADR 0004) ===
- Package: @opencode-ai/plugin v1.17.11 (peerDependency). Backend is Bun/JS in-process (plan §2).
- Discovery/load: the SHIPPED source lives in this repo at plugins/adlc-opencode/ (mirroring plugins/adlc-codex, plugins/adlc-pi); /adlc-init copies/symlinks it into the user's .opencode/plugin/adlc-opencode/ and registers it in .opencode/opencode.json (plan §4.1, Phase A). OpenCode loads the pre-bundled dist/index.js.
- Edit-interception hook: "tool.execute.before", async (input, output) => {...}. VERIFY-FIRST and pin in ADR 0004: (i) whether the edited path is input.args.filePath or output.args.filePath (docs vs gist conflict) — capture a real edit AND write payload; (ii) the full set of file-mutating tool names in v1.17.11 (edit/write/patch/multiedit/apply_patch).
- CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT-CAPABILITY GATE (plan §Phase D — resolves the earlier 'does throw abort the write?' question): the in-session hook MUST NOT be labelled/treated as enforcing unless the installed OpenCode SDK supports `onFailure: deny` AND a runtime capability probe confirms it. If unsupported, the hook is ADVISORY only and preflight FAILS CLOSED unless `allowAdvisoryHooks: true` is explicitly configured. The unbypassable layer remains the CI gate (already built).
- Workspace root: PIN which plugin context field (project/directory/worktree) is the repo root for locating .adlc/.

=== RAIL CONTRACT — delegate to @adlc/core, preserve sibling semantics ===
The thin adapter (rails-checker.ts) maps OpenCode hook args to @adlc/core and must preserve the contract both sibling hooks implement (plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs, plugins/adlc-pi/index.ts):
1. Active ticket via process.env.ADLC_TICKET OR .adlc/current-ticket.json; conflict => fail closed.
2. Enforce only when process.env.ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT === '1'; else no-op.
3. Rails = the SINGLE active ticket's rails PLUS implicit trust-root rails '.adlc/tickets.json' and '.adlc/current-ticket.json'. NOT a union across tickets.
4. No-op fail-safe when .adlc/tickets.json absent, enforcement off, no active ticket, or empty declared rails (trust-root still frozen).
5. On a rail match, deny via the SDK's onFailure:deny contract (per the capability gate above), naming the rail + ticket.

=== DELIVERABLES (this MVP increment only) ===
1. plugins/adlc-opencode/ — Node package mirroring the sibling integrations: package.json (@adlc/opencode-package, type module, peerDependency @opencode-ai/plugin >=1.17.11, dependency @adlc/core), index.ts (the Plugin named export wiring tool.execute.before), rails-checker.ts (thin adapter importing @adlc/core rails logic — NO inlined re-implementation), a pre-bundled dist/index.js, and skill/adlc.md (the phase-routing discovery skill, copied/adapted from the sibling skill sentinels IF OpenCode's skill format matches; verify first).
2. scripts/opencode-install-smoke.mjs — mirrors scripts/codex-install-smoke.mjs / scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs: validate the plugin package shape, the dist bundle, the hook wiring, skill registration, and that the deny path delegates to @adlc/core. Must not require the opencode binary and must not mutate the user environment.
3. docs/integrations/opencode.md — replace the 'no integration exists yet' stub with a real landing doc that LINKS the authoritative plan (docs/opencode-integration-plan.md) and docs/opencode.md, documents this MVP increment + the two-layer enforcement (advisory in-session hook gated on onFailure:deny + the already-built mandatory CI gate), Install (local verification via the smoke test), the Formal ADLC Coverage table, and Gaps (the unbuilt Phases A/B/C/E below; the deferred .opencode/plugin path protection).
4. docs/adr/0004-adlc-opencode-integration.md — formal ADR pointing to the plan as the detailed design, pinning the resolved API facts (i)-(ii), the onFailure:deny capability gate, and a Threat Model section (the in-session bypass surface; CI gate as mitigation).

OUT OF SCOPE (now authored as follow-on tickets T2 Phase A / T3 Phase B / T4 Phase C / T5 Phase E — note them in the ADR Gaps, do not build here): the full slash-command suite (/adlc-ticket../adlc-maintain), the keyless two-phase LLM bridge, the advisory session hooks, the 5-lens prosecutor subagents + verifier, and the .opencode/plugin path-protection CI follow-up.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: `node scripts/opencode-install-smoke.mjs .` exits 0 and reports the plugin package, dist bundle, hook wiring, and skill registration valid. VERIFY: run it; assert exit 0.
- AC2: The deny path delegates to @adlc/core (single source of truth) and does NOT re-implement glob/rail matching inline. VERIFY: smoke test asserts rails-checker.ts imports @adlc/core; a grep confirms no inlined globMatch/canonicalizePath copy in the plugin.
- AC3 (enforcement proof, runs by default, no opencode binary): a unit test at plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs invokes the REAL exported tool.execute.before handler with a CAPTURED real payload, under `node --test`, covering and passing: (a) no-op when .adlc/tickets.json absent; (b) no-op when ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT != '1'; (c) no-op when no active ticket; (d) DENY an edit AND a write to the active ticket's rail; (e) DENY an edit to .adlc/tickets.json (trust-root); (f) a DIFFERENT ticket's rail does NOT block; (g) conflicting ADLC_TICKET vs current-ticket.json fails closed; (h) when the SDK capability probe reports no onFailure:deny support, the hook is advisory and preflight fails closed unless allowAdvisoryHooks is set. VERIFY: test exercises each via the real handler and exits 0.
- AC4: docs/integrations/opencode.md no longer contains 'no integration exists yet', links docs/opencode-integration-plan.md, and has Install + Formal ADLC Coverage table + Gaps. VERIFY: grep for absence of the banner, presence of the plan link, and the three headings.
- AC5: docs/adr/0004 exists, references the plan, pins the API facts + onFailure:deny gate, and has a '## Threat Model' section. VERIFY: file exists; grep for @opencode-ai/plugin + tool.execute.before + 'onFailure' + '## Threat Model'.
- AC6: No sibling integration regresses. VERIFY: `node scripts/codex-install-smoke.mjs .` and `node scripts/claude-code-plugin-smoke.mjs .` both exit 0.
- AC7: The existing CI backstop is acknowledged, not duplicated. VERIFY: docs/integrations/opencode.md states the unbypassable CI layer is docs/ci/rails-guard.yml (already implemented on opencode-integration) and this ticket adds no competing CI workflow; grep confirms no new .github/workflows or docs/ci file is created by this ticket.

Suppressions are denied. PREREQUISITE: this ticket's build depends on the opencode-integration design + @adlc/core + CI backstop being available on the working base (merge/rebase opencode-integration to main first, or build atop it). If that base is absent, STOP and escalate rather than re-deriving the design.

tickets.title: Schema bedrock: definition-driven validator + generated JSON Schemas
tickets.body:
Build the foundation of @adlc/ticket-sync per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-27-external-ticketing-sync-design.md (sections 'Schema bedrock', 'Hard constraints', field-definition table). Create packages/ticket-sync as a zero-runtime-dependency package (CONVENTIONS rule 1; Node 18+ built-ins only) WITHOUT editing packages/core (CONVENTIONS rule 2 — core is frozen). Deliver: lib/schema.mjs (single declarative field definition = source of truth), lib/validate.mjs (definition-driven validator over the rich schema), lib/canonical.mjs (canonical JSON: sorted keys, LF, stable number formatting, CRLF-insensitive equality), scripts/gen-schema.mjs (emits schemas/adlc-ticket.schema.json, adlc-block.schema.json, adlc-config.schema.json, adlc-sync-state.schema.json from the definition), and the committed schema files.

Acceptance criteria (each verifiable):
1. `npm test` green for packages/ticket-sync/test/{schema,validate,canonical}.test.mjs.
2. Drift gate: test regenerates schemas in-memory and asserts byte-equality with the committed schemas/*.json; editing the definition without regenerating fails the test (verify by mutating the definition in a scratch run).
3. Cross-validator agreement: a corpus of tickets core's validateTicket accepts is also accepted by the rich validator on shared fields (asymmetric subset direction).
4. No file under packages/core is modified (verify: `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/core` is empty).
5. Package declares zero runtime dependencies (verify: no 'dependencies' beyond @adlc/* in package.json).

tickets.title: Fenced JSON block codec (parse/serialize, fail-closed)
tickets.body:
Implement lib/block.mjs in @adlc/ticket-sync per the spec sections 'The block' and 'Validity Gate' (block cases). The block is JSON (JSON.parse — no YAML, zero-dep) wrapped in reserved HTML-comment sentinels `<!-- adlc:begin v=1 key=<uuid> -->` ... `<!-- adlc:end -->`. parseBlock(body) returns {prefix, block, suffix, version, key, formatErrors}; serializeBlock(prose{prefix,suffix}, fields) reproduces the body. Field validation delegates to T1's validator (no second schema). Depends on T1.

Acceptance criteria:
1. packages/ticket-sync/test/block.test.mjs green covering: lossless round-trip (prefix AND suffix prose preserved verbatim); missing/duplicate/unbalanced sentinels -> fail closed with an error naming the offending line; garbled JSON -> fail closed; present-but-invalid block (e.g. malformed rails) -> fail closed (NEVER degrade to 'no rails'); `$schema` key excluded from canonical equality; sentinel `v` greater than supported max -> fail closed.
2. A human-authored ```json fence in prose outside the sentinels is ignored.
3. Body model {prefix, block, suffix} is preserved across a parse->serialize cycle.

tickets.title: Pull: GitHub read adapter, 3-way reconcile, Validity Gate, sidecar, store
tickets.body:
Implement `adlc ticket pull` (dry-run by default; --write applies) per the spec data-flow 'Pull', 'Sidecar', 'Validity Gate', 'Sync vs the rails trust root', and 'Lock + atomic write'. Deliver: lib/gh.mjs (execFile wrapper — argv only, no shell, C4), lib/providers/github.mjs (read/map), lib/provider.mjs (interface, no registry), lib/reconcile.mjs (pure 3-way base/local/remote; base from sidecar syncedHash; missing/corrupt base fails safe to CONFLICT), lib/config.mjs (+ adlc-config validation, repo auto-detect, issue selector), lib/store.mjs (writeTicketsAtomic + mkdir lock sharing .adlc/tickets.lock; sidecar .adlc/ticket-sync.state.json gitignored rebuildable cache), lib/rails-guard-sync.mjs (rails superset / scope subset guard + forensic record), and register the `ticket` tool in packages/cli/lib/registry.mjs. Single repo-qualified id space gh:owner/repo#n, owner/repo lowercased to match loadTickets equality; unresolved edges FAIL CLOSED (no silent drop); pagination explicit (truncation -> exit 1, never deletion). Depends on T2.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/{reconcile,github,config,store,validity,rails-guard-sync}.test.mjs green; all offline via an injected gh runner with canned --json fixtures.
2. reconcile: remote-only/local-only/both-changed(conflict)/both-equal(converged); local-only ticket survives pull; out-of-selection survives.
3. Validity Gate: id normalization unifies T<n>/gh: spellings; an unresolved edges[].to fails closed (exit 2), not dropped; resolution-checked set == bytes written.
4. rails-guard-sync: rails non-superset and scope-widen refused without --allow-rail-narrowing; forensic record written.
5. pull is dry-run without --write (verify no file mutation); exit codes 0/1/2 per matrix.

tickets.title: Push + create: write-back, idempotent create, status outcomes
tickets.body:
Implement `adlc ticket push` and `adlc ticket sync` (dry-run by default; --write applies) per the spec data-flow 'Push'. Deliver: lib/outcomes.mjs (reduce .adlc/manifest.jsonl -> per-ticket status: latest-per-gate, verdict=latest P5 entry, no P5 -> no pass label), lib/status-render.mjs (labels mutually-exclusive within statusLabels + a canonical timestamp-free status comment; both display-only, never authoritative), and github write ops (updateIssueBody, ensureLabels, upsertStatusComment, createIssue). Create is idempotent: stable sentinel key, adopt off the already-paginated pull list (not the eventually-consistent search index), persist {nodeId,number} into pendingCreates before id-reassignment, >1 key match fails closed; on create reassign id T<n>->gh:owner/repo#n, rewrite every edges[].to store-wide, migrate manifest evidence to the new id. Transfer/renumber reuses the same reassign+edge-rewrite path. Depends on T3.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/outcomes.test.mjs green: multiple verdicts (latest wins), none (no fabricated pass), per-gate latest.
2. test/github.test.mjs idempotency: push twice against a recording fake -> second run makes no mutating calls; create adoption finds an existing keyed issue; a simulated lost local write does NOT duplicate; id reassignment rewrites edge references.
3. push is dry-run without --write; partial failure -> per-issue result list, exit 1.

tickets.title: Doctor: read-only, offline health checks
tickets.body:
Implement `adlc ticket doctor` (read-only always; --json) per the spec 'doctor — read-only, offline (MVP)'. A flat list of offline checks; exit 2 if any error else 0. No --fix, no network, no registry (deferred to a follow-up spec). Checks: .adlc/config.json valid against adlc-config.schema.json; tickets.json loads via @adlc/core loadTickets with no errors (dup id / dangling edge / cycle / schema); committed JSON Schemas == regenerated (bedrock drift); sidecar valid, no two ids map to one nodeId, every synced ticket has a syncedHash, no stale pendingCreates; stale .adlc/tickets.lock (age-guarded, reported not removed). Depends on T3 (config/store/validity/sidecar).

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/doctor.test.mjs green: each check has a failing AND a passing fixture; exit codes correct (0 healthy, 2 problems).
2. doctor performs zero network calls and zero writes (verify with an injected gh runner that throws on use, and a read-only assertion).

3. README links resolve and match the shipped commands.

tickets.title: Fix create idempotency: selector-independent crash recovery + edge rewrite before remote serialize
tickets.body:
Two cross-model (codex/GPT) adversarial-review findings on the merged T9 push/create path (PR #33). FIX both with TDD.

Finding 1 (HIGH, duplicate issues under the DEFAULT label-scoped selector): createIssue attaches no label, and the create adoption scan only searches the selector-scoped issue list and ignores the nodeId/number already stored in pendingCreates. A crash after the remote create but before renderAndPush labels the issue leaves an UNLABELED orphan that the next run's label-scoped listIssues cannot see, so adoption misses and a DUPLICATE issue is created. Fix: (a) when pendingCreates[key] carries a number/nodeId, adopt that issue DIRECTLY (verify via issue view) instead of relying on the selector-scoped body scan; (b) attach the configured createLabel at create time so the new issue immediately belongs to the selected set. The body-key scan remains the fallback when pendingCreates was lost.

Finding 2 (HIGH, stale edges published to the tracker): the create loop reads `desired = pickBlock(t)` from the ORIGINAL localTickets snapshot, but reassignId rewrites the working `tickets` array. A dependent ticket created later (T8 edges->T7) serializes its STALE T<n> edge into the remote issue body + syncedHash while tickets.json gets the rewritten gh: edge, leaving the tracker an invalid sync source until the next push. Fix: in the create loop, derive `desired` from the CURRENT reassigned working `tickets` entry (by id), not the stale snapshot.

Acceptance criteria:
1. test/github.test.mjs: the stateful fake's listIssues HONORS the label selector (only returns issues carrying the selected labels). A new test: create succeeds, labeling is skipped/crashes (unlabeled orphan) -> a re-run with a label-scoped selector ADOPTS via pendingCreates (no second `issue create` call); assert exactly one remote issue.
2. test/github.test.mjs: createIssue attaches the configured createLabel at create time (the new issue is in the label-scoped selection immediately).
3. test/github.test.mjs: multi-create T7 + T8(edges->T7) under --write -> assert T8's REMOTE issue body block carries edge to gh:owner/repo#<T7-number>, NOT 'T7'; and its sidecar syncedHash matches the rewritten block.
4. Full suite green; re-prosecute with adlc:prosecutor (P5) to CLEAR; THEN a cross-model adversarial-review pass (codex) before merge (the lesson from this finding).

tickets.title: Consolidate the five replicated ADLC phase routers into a single source of truth
tickets.body:
PROBLEM. The ADLC phase-router content (the "where am I / which gate" map plus per-phase gate descriptions) is duplicated across five harness plugins in three file conventions:
  - plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md   (prose phase list)
  - plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc/SKILL.md          (prose phase list)
  - plugins/adlc-pi/skills/adlc/SKILL.md             (prose phase list)
  - plugins/adlc-opencode/skill/adlc.md              (table + prose)
  - plugins/adlc-cursor/rules/adlc.mdc               (Cursor .mdc table)
This replication is a drift hazard: an edit can update some harnesses and miss others. It happened during PR #55 (opencode and cursor were initially omitted from a router edit), and PR #55's whole-branch review (independent agy and opus reviewers) flagged the replication as a LOW maintenance hazard with the recommendation to consolidate to a single source of truth.

GOAL. Define ONE canonical source for the phase-router content and generate each harness's router file from it, so a single edit propagates to all five and a CI check fails if any harness drifts. Preserve each file's required format and front-matter (prose for the three SKILL.md files; a table for the cursor .mdc and opencode adlc.md).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification method):
AC1 - A single canonical source file exists (e.g. docs/router/phase-router.yaml or a module under packages/) holding the phase map + per-phase gate text + the adversarial-review discoverability content. Verify: the file exists and is the input the generator reads (grep the generator for its path).
AC2 - A generator/build step emits all five harness router files from the canonical source, preserving each file's format and any YAML/frontmatter. Verify: run the generator on a clean checkout, then `git diff --exit-code` on the five router paths returns 0 (generated output equals committed).
AC3 - A CI-runnable drift check fails when any harness router diverges from the canonical source. Verify: hand-edit one generated router, run the check, assert non-zero exit; regenerate, assert exit 0.
AC4 - The PR #55 discoverability content survives consolidation: every generated router names `adversarial-review` at P1/P3/P5 and contains the exact phrase `exit 0 = SHIP`. Verify: after generation, grep each of the five files for `adversarial-review` and `exit 0 = SHIP`; all five match.
AC5 - No routing regression: each generated router carries the same phase->gate mapping it had pre-consolidation. Verify: compare the semantic phase->gate content of each generated router against its pre-consolidation version (git show HEAD:<path>); differences are limited to formatting/source-derivation, not routing changes.

CONTEXT. Related to PR #55 (ADR-0008 adversarial-review coverage map). The router files were last edited there; use their current committed form as the content baseline to extract into the canonical source. Suppressions are denied.

tickets.title: Add adversarial-review discoverability to the adlc-antigravity phase router
tickets.body:
PROBLEM. PR #55 added an adversarial-review loop discoverability block (references at P1/P3/P5 and the phrase `exit 0 = SHIP`) to the ADLC phase routers of five harnesses. The sixth harness, adlc-antigravity (merged separately in PR #53), was not covered: its phase router `plugins/adlc-antigravity/skills/adlc/SKILL.md` is a full-map prose router (~20 phase->gate pairs, `---` frontmatter) but contains ZERO `adversarial-review` mentions. Operators on Antigravity therefore see no guidance to reach for the cross-model ship/no-ship loop at P1/P3/P5.

GOAL. Bring the antigravity router in line with the other five (specifically claude-code, the closest full-map prose analogue): add the adversarial-review references at the P1 (design review), P3 (rail-selection adequacy), and P5 (built code, >=2 providers) entries, plus a short 'adversarial-review loop' note (cross-model + fresh-context + loop-until-SHIP; flags `--verify`, `--loop`, `--providers`; the exact phrase `exit 0 = SHIP`; an `npx adversarial-review` invoke hint; and reference ADR-0008 by NAME, no repo-relative link since routers ship as installed plugins). Match the file's existing prose voice; do not use the unsupported `adversarial-review <spec.md>` positional or a `--loop` command for P1/P3 artifact review (see PR #55's corrected guidance: P1/P3 reviews are `--prompt-only`/diff-based today because `--input` is deferred).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 - `grep -c 'adversarial-review' plugins/adlc-antigravity/skills/adlc/SKILL.md` returns a value >= 1 and `grep -c 'exit 0 = SHIP' plugins/adlc-antigravity/skills/adlc/SKILL.md` returns >= 1. Verify by running both greps.
AC2 - The references appear at P1, P3 and P5. Verify: `grep -nE 'P1|P3|P5' plugins/adlc-antigravity/skills/adlc/SKILL.md` shows the adversarial-review mentions co-located with those phases.

Events pinned against docs: preToolUse (blockable, JSON stdin/stdout, permission allow|deny|ask), afterFileEdit (observational, cannot block), beforeShellExecution, beforeReadFile. === MODES TO ADD (all advisory except buildgate, which mirrors rails' best-effort deny) ===
1. buildgate (preToolUse, second entry): port the fitness-to-build gate (issue #48; reference implementation plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs buildgate mode). Deny a structured edit when the active ticket is high-risk AND the session context-fitness signal is degraded, unless ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 with an audited gate-manifest record. Context-fitness input: Cursor hooks do not receive a transcript_path; derive depth from a session tool-call counter persisted under .adlc/ by the hook itself (document the proxy's weakness honestly) or accept ADLC_BUILD_GATE_DEPTH env input.
2. flail (afterFileEdit, piggyback in adlc-audit.mjs): after the rail audit, run the flail heuristics (packages/flail-detector primitives) over the hook's own persisted recent-edits window; advisory stderr notice only.

Phase 1a of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md (committed on this branch — READ IT FIRST; it is the contract). Fixes the correctness core of plugins/adlc-pi and completes the ADR-0004 core-delegation work that was done for cursor/opencode (#97/#102) but skipped for pi.

=== VERIFIED pi API FACTS (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent v0.80.3) ===
- pi loads extensions as TypeScript via jiti; there is NO compile step. The checked-in plugins/adlc-pi/index.js is a hand-compiled artifact and must be deleted.
- CRITICAL BUG: the `before_agent_start` result `{systemPrompt}` REPLACES the turn's system prompt (chained across extensions); the documented pattern is `event.systemPrompt + "..."` (see BeforeAgentStartEventResult in the package's dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts and docs/extensions.md, which shows `systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + "\n\nExtra instructions..."`). Current index.ts returns ONLY the ADLC doctrine block — wiping pi's entire built-in system prompt whenever a ticket is active — and only an error banner on config load errors.

tickets.title: pi Phase 1b: shrink tool_result blast radius, operative-only suppression scan, live-deny CI proof, docs truth v1
tickets.body:
Phase 1b of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md (the contract — READ IT FIRST). Builds on T20's restructured plugins/adlc-pi (thin index.ts + lib/*.mjs delegating to @adlc/core). Shrinks the reactive gate's blast radius, makes the suppression scan operative-only, proves the deny path live in CI, and lands docs truth pass v1.

=== CONTEXT (current defects, live-verified) ===
- The tool_result handler runs `git add -N .` on every mutating tool result (pollutes the user's index), diffs the WHOLE worktree against HEAD (attributing pre-session/user edits to the agent), and reverts violations with whole-file `git checkout HEAD -- <f>` — destroying uncommitted user work in that file.
- The suppression scan does naive substring matching over added lines, flagging markers inside docs/strings/fences. @adlc/core exports fence/operative-line helpers (computeFencedLines, matchFenceOpen, isFenceClose); the P7 text-scanning-gate lens (docs/review-lenses/) is the standard: derive operative-vs-inert authoritatively, normalize line endings, fail closed.
- The active ticket is resolved only at session_start; a ticket activated mid-session is invisible until /ticket is run manually.
- pi RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`) speaks JSONL over stdin/stdout with STRICT LF framing — Node's readline is documented non-compliant; use a raw stream reader.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Snapshot-based targeted revert: at tool_call time for write/edit, snapshot the target file's content (or its absence); on a rail/suppression violation detected in tool_result, restore exactly that snapshot — never `git checkout HEAD`. Scope diff inspection to the paths the tool touched; only bash results may trigger a repo-wide diff. Replace `git add -N .` with untracked-file detection via `git status --porcelain`. The gate never modifies files the tool did not write.
2. Suppression scan operative-only: use @adlc/core fence/comment derivation over the added lines of touched files only; inert text (e.g. fenced code blocks in .md) is not flagged; when operative-vs-inert cannot be derived, fail closed (flag). Keep the `allow-suppression:` body protocol and the allowedSuppressions ticket field.
3. Live ticket lifecycle: re-resolve the active ticket on turn_start via an mtime check on .adlc/current-ticket.json plus env re-read; preserve the fail-closed posture on load errors.
4. Live deny proof: scripts/pi-live-deny.mjs creates a temp git repo containing a ticket with a frozen rail, launches `pi --mode rpc` (from a pinned devDependency) with the extension loaded, drives a prompt that attempts a rail edit, and asserts the tool call is blocked with a GATE message. Wire it into .github/workflows/ci.yml inside the existing required job (private-repo free plan cannot add required checks — mirror the rails-guard CI fallback pattern). If driving a real model in CI is infeasible, drive the RPC session with a scripted provider/model stub — the assertion that matters is extension-level deny, not model behavior.
5. Docs truth v1: fix the README.md line calling this the "Raspberry Pi harness"; add a "Shipped vs design intent" ledger to docs/integrations/pi.md consistent with the spec (no capability claimed shipped without a runtime caller).

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: test: a file carries uncommitted user edits; a gated write to it violates a rail; after the revert the user edits are intact and only the tool's write is undone. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC2: `grep -rn "add -N" plugins/adlc-pi` is empty; creation of an untracked file at a rail path via bash is still detected and denied (test). VERIFY: grep + node --test.
- AC3: a suppression marker inside a fenced block of a .md file is NOT flagged; the same marker on an operative code line IS flagged and reverted per deliverable 1. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC4: test simulating ticket activation after session start: the next turn_start picks it up (doctrine injected, gating active). VERIFY: node --test.
- AC5: `node scripts/pi-live-deny.mjs` exits 0 locally; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it in the required job. VERIFY: run the script + grep ci.yml.
- AC6: `grep -i raspberry README.md` is empty; docs/integrations/pi.md contains a "Shipped vs design intent" section. VERIFY: grep.

Suppressions are denied. Do not modify sibling plugin directories or packages/core (frozen for this ticket — fence helpers already exist there).

tickets.title: pi Phase 2a: build-gate context-rot backstop on ctx.getContextUsage() + flail advisory
tickets.body:
Phase 2 items 2.1 + 2.2 of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md (READ IT FIRST — it is the contract). Builds on the merged Phase 1 plugin (plugins/adlc-pi: thin index.ts + lib/*.mjs, decisions in lib/rails-checker.mjs, wiring in lib/extension.mjs, snapshot gate in lib/reactive-gate.mjs; wiring tests drive handlers through a fake pi object — mirror that test harness).

=== VERIFIED pi API FACTS (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.80.3, devDependency installed — authoritative types in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts) ===
- Event-handler ctx exposes `getContextUsage() -> { tokens, contextWindow, percent }` — a REAL context-fitness signal (no sibling harness has one; opencode uses a tool-call-count proxy).
- `session_compact` (notify) fires after compaction; `session_before_compact` carries `{ reason: "manual"|"threshold"|"overflow" }`. Compaction due to threshold/overflow IS the context-rot event.
- `tool_execution_end` fires after every tool run (see types.d.ts for its payload); `pi.sendMessage({customType, content}, {deliverAs: "steer"})` queues an advisory the model sees before its next LLM call.
- Handlers can block only in `tool_call` (return {block:true, reason}).

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Build-gate backstop (spec 2.1): a second enforcing check in the tool_call handler that denies STRUCTURED mutations (write/edit) when (a) the active ticket's risk tier is 'high' AND (b) the session is context-degraded. Delegate the decision to the canonical @adlc/build-gate modules — computeRiskTier from @adlc/build-gate/lib/risk.mjs, decideBuildGate from @adlc/build-gate/lib/decide.mjs, recordOverride from @adlc/build-gate/lib/override.mjs — exactly as plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/build-gate.mjs does (read it as the porting reference; do NOT fork decision logic). Pi-specific parts: the degradation signal is ctx.getContextUsage().percent >= a threshold (export DEFAULT_CONTEXT_PERCENT_THRESHOLD = 80, override via ADLC_BUILD_GATE_CONTEXT_PCT), OR a session_compact event with reason threshold/overflow observed this session. Activation follows pi's model (active ticket = the switch; no ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT). Bypass contract: ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 allows ONLY when recordOverride durably records to .adlc/manifest.jsonl (decideBuildGate enforces this — an unrecordable override is refused).
2. Flail advisory (spec 2.2): port plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/flail.mjs — synthesize the "Editing <path>" lines from pi tool events and delegate churn detection to detectEditChurn from @adlc/flail-detector/lib/signals.mjs (canonical; do not re-implement). pi is single-session per process: a bounded window (default 200 entries) suffices; no multi-session LRU needed. On a file newly crossing the churn threshold, warn once per file via ctx.ui.notify AND pi.sendMessage(..., {deliverAs:'steer'}) so the model itself is steered. Advisory only — never blocks.
3. Wire both into lib/extension.mjs with the same fail-closed-on-broken-ticket posture as the rail gate; new lib modules lib/build-gate.mjs and lib/flail.mjs, each unit-tested through the fake-pi wiring harness.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: with a high-risk ticket (risk tier derived by computeRiskTier from the ticket, e.g. rails matching RISK_TIER_PATTERNS) and a fake ctx whose getContextUsage() returns percent >= threshold, a write tool_call is DENIED with a reason naming the build gate; the same call with percent below threshold is ALLOWED; a normal-risk ticket is ALLOWED at any percent. VERIFY: node --test wiring tests.
- AC2: a session_compact event (reason 'overflow' or 'threshold') marks the session degraded even when getContextUsage() reports a low percent (post-compaction tokens shrink — compaction itself is the rot event); next high-risk structured mutation is DENIED. A 'manual' compaction does NOT degrade. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC3: ADLC_BUILD_GATE_BYPASS=1 allows the blocked call and appends an override record to .adlc/manifest.jsonl; when the record cannot be written (unwritable dir), the call stays DENIED. VERIFY: node --test asserting both the allow+ledger-line and the failed-record deny.
- AC4: editing the same file >= 3 times within the window emits exactly ONE steer message + ONE notify for that file (no repeat warnings); a fourth edit of a DIFFERENT file emits none. VERIFY: node --test on the fake pi capturing sendMessage calls.
- AC5: build-gate and flail state do not leak across reloads: after session_start fires again (reason 'resume'/'new'), the degraded flag and churn window reset. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0; `node scripts/pi-live-deny.mjs` still passes (the new gate must not break the live rail deny).

Suppressions are denied. Marker strings, if any test needs them, must be assembled by concatenation (see plugins/adlc-pi/test/reactive-gate.test.mjs precedent) so text-scanning gates stay quiet on the diff. Do not modify sibling plugin directories, packages/core, packages/build-gate, or packages/flail-detector — pi consumes them as-is; if a canonical module genuinely lacks something, STOP and escalate rather than forking.

tickets.title: pi Phase 2b: session evidence rail, custom-tool coverage, user_bash advisory, position-aware suppression diff
tickets.body:
Phase 2 items 2.3 + 2.4 + 2.5 of docs/specs/pi-native-flush.md plus the banked P5 finding in the spec's Phase 2 preamble (READ THE SPEC FIRST). Builds on T22's extension wiring.

=== VERIFIED pi API FACTS (0.80.3; types in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts) ===
- `pi.appendEntry(customType, data?)` persists a custom entry into the pi session file (NOT sent to the LLM); reconstruct on session_start via ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()/getBranch().
- `pi.setLabel(entryId, label?)` bookmarks an entry — labels are visible in pi's /tree view.
- `user_bash` event fires when the HUMAN runs `!`/`!!` shell commands: { command, excludeFromContext, cwd }. Human commands bypass tool gates by design.
- `tool_call` fires for custom third-party tools too (CustomToolCallEvent: toolName is a plain string, input is Record<string,unknown>); isToolCallEventType narrows built-ins.
- @adlc/core exports appendEntry(name, entry, dir?) (the .adlc ledger writer, used for manifest.jsonl) — distinct from pi's session appendEntry; use BOTH per deliverable 1.

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Evidence rail (spec 2.4): every gate event (rail deny, scope deny, shell deny, suppression revert, build-gate deny, flail warning) is recorded (a) into the pi session file via pi.appendEntry('adlc-gate-event', {...}) so it survives in the session tree, AND (b) mirrored to .adlc/manifest.jsonl via @adlc/core's ledger appendEntry. Where the pi API yields an entry id, setLabel the violation entries (label like 'ADLC deny: <rail>') so /tree shows enforcement history. Recording must never crash a gate: failures degrade to a ctx.ui.notify warning.
2. Custom-tool coverage (spec 2.5): the tool_call gate currently keys on write/edit/bash names. Extend: for any OTHER tool name, extract path-like string values from event.input (keys named path/file/filePath/target or any string value that resolves inside the repo); if any resolves to a frozen rail (railHit) → deny. If the tool name is unknown AND the input carries NO extractable path AND the tool is not in a small READONLY allowlist (read/grep/find/ls — see opencode's READONLY_TOOLS precedent) → leave it ungated but record an 'unvetted-tool' evidence entry (pi custom tools legitimately include no-file-target tools; the snapshot/diff reactive gate plus CI remain the backstop — this matches spec 2.5's layered posture, and hard fail-closed for every unknown tool would break pi package ecosystems).
3. user_bash advisory (spec 2.3): on a user_bash event whose command classifies as a mutation touching a frozen rail (reuse checkShellCommand — decision only), do NOT block (human override is legitimate) but notify a warning and record an evidence entry marking a human rail mutation.
4. Position-aware suppression diff (banked P5 finding): diffAddedLines' multiset semantics miss a pre-existing identical marker line RELOCATED from inert to operative position (e.g. moved out of a fenced block). Fix: in scanAddedLines (or a successor), when a file's new content contains a marker on an operative line, flag it if that marker was NOT present on any operative line of the OLD content — i.e. compare operative-marker sets before/after rather than relying only on added-line counts. Keep the existing added-lines path for performance; the operative-set comparison runs only when the quick scan found markers anywhere in the new content.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: a rail deny and a suppression revert each produce (a) a pi session appendEntry call with customType 'adlc-gate-event' and (b) a line in .adlc/manifest.jsonl; a failing ledger write does not prevent the deny itself. VERIFY: node --test with the fake pi capturing appendEntry, plus a real temp-dir manifest assertion.
- AC2: a synthetic third-party tool call {toolName:'write_file', input:{file:'<rail path>'}} is DENIED; the same tool against an in-scope path is not blocked; a no-path unknown tool ('run_linter', input:{}) is allowed AND recorded as 'unvetted-tool'. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC3: a symlink passed through a custom tool's path arg is resolved (railHit's symlink awareness applies) and denied. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC4: user_bash with a rail-mutating command produces a warning notice + evidence entry and does NOT block; a read-only user_bash produces nothing. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC5: a file whose old content had a marker inside a fenced .mdx block and whose new content has the SAME marker line moved outside the fence is FLAGGED, even though the multiset of lines is unchanged; the reverse move (operative → fenced) is NOT flagged. VERIFY: node --test.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0; `node scripts/pi-live-deny.mjs` passes.

Suppressions are denied; assemble marker fixtures by concatenation (see reactive-gate.test.mjs precedent). Do not modify sibling plugins or packages/** — if shared logic needs a change, STOP and escalate.

In non-TUI modes (rpc/json/print) dialogs resolve undefined — every command must degrade gracefully (notify + return, never hang or throw).

1. Prompt templates in plugins/adlc-pi/prompts/ registered via package.json `pi.prompts: ["./prompts"]`: adlc-spec.md (P0–P2 workflow), adlc-decompose.md (P2), adlc-verify-build.md (build-gate/preflight), adlc-prosecute.md (P5 evidence recording), adlc-distill.md (P7), adlc-maintain.md (decay checks). tickets.body:
Make installing the OpenCode integration a one-command, self-healing experience. Full context: docs/specs/opencode-integration-continuation.md §T-B.

=== DEFECT TO FIX FIRST (TDD: failing test first) ===
plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/scaffold.mjs ensurePluginRegistered() registers the npm name "@adlc/opencode-package" in opencode.json's plugin array, but the package is "private": true and NOT on npm. tickets.title: OpenCode Phase 4b: deterministic P5 runner — adlc_prosecute native tool with locked-down child sessions
tickets.body:
Make OpenCode's P5 prosecution deterministic first-party code instead of model-driven orchestration — the leapfrog no other integration has. Full context: docs/specs/opencode-integration-continuation.md §T-E and docs/specs/opencode-native-flush.md §4.3. Depends on T31.

=== DESIGN (verified against @opencode-ai/plugin 1.17.17) ===
Register a second native tool adlc_prosecute (alongside adlc_gate in index.mjs, same lazy tool.schema import pattern). Its execute() drives the fan-out → dedupe → verify → loop-until-dry protocol IN CODE, using the already-tested decision helpers in plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/prosecutor.mjs (they are currently consumed only by the model-driven /adlc-prosecute command). Child lens/verifier sessions via client.session.create({parentID}) + session.prompt with:
- per-call system override carrying the lens prompt (agent/prosecutor-*.md content),
- tools:{...} enable/disable map so lens sessions get NO write tools (edit/write/patch/bash disabled) — a lens can read, never mutate,
- structured verdicts via a registered verdict tool schema. NOTE: session.prompt has NO outputFormat field at 1.17.17 (the flush spec's assumption was falsified; the correction is recorded in docs/specs/opencode-integration-continuation.md) — the verdict tool IS the structured-output mechanism; fall back to fenced-JSON parsing of text parts (fail-closed on unparseable, mirroring lib/keyless-bridge.mjs).
/adlc-prosecute command becomes a thin invoker of the tool, keeping the prose protocol as fallback when the tool is unavailable.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
AC1: unit tests drive runProsecution() with a mocked client through: multi-lens fan-out, dedupe of identical findings, verifier confirm/refute, loop-until-dry termination (2 consecutive dry rounds), and hard bounds (max rounds / max child sessions) (verify: node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/).
AC2: lens child sessions provably cannot write: test asserts the tools map passed to session.prompt disables every mutating tool; a live-proof assertion drives a lens session and confirms a write attempt is rejected (verify: unit test + extension of scripts/opencode-live-tool.mjs).
AC3: seeded-defect convergence: live proof plants a known defect, runs adlc_prosecute, asserts the finding surfaces and the loop terminates without the host model orchestrating (verify: live script exit 0 in CI, pinned version).
AC4: unparseable verdict → fail-closed (finding kept, marked unverified), never silently dropped (verify: unit test).
AC5: /adlc-prosecute command doc updated to invoke the tool first with prose fallback (verify: read command/adlc-prosecute.md).
